children.title: A slot is an octave
lines: ONE SLOT = ONE OCTAVE of the keybed.
The 32 pads are laid out like a keyboard, bottom row first:
row 1  C  D  E  F  G  A  B  C   (white keys)
row 2  .  C# D# .  F# G# A# .   (black keys, above them)
row 3  C  D  E  F  G  A  B  C   (white keys)
row 4  .  C# D# .  F# G# A# .   (black keys, above them)
The six pads shown as '.' are where a piano has no key; they do nothing.
The slot selected with the Slot knob owns the LOWER pair of rows.
The pair above it is the NEXT slot up. So with Slot 5 the surface
shows slots 5 and 6, with Slot 6 it shows 6 and 7, and so on: the
knob pages the pads up through the sample slots.
Inside an octave the KEY is what sets the pitch: the octave's C
plays the sample at its own speed, the keys above it play it
higher - up to the B, at 1.89x. Pressing the C of the upper pair
is the same as the C at the end of the lower pair.
The Octave knob transposes the whole keybed, one octave a step.
Slot 15 is the recording buffer: whatever the Recorder page's take
left there plays from the keybed like any other slot.

children.title: Loading your own samples
lines: Samples page: Slot picks the slot, Sample opens the browser, and
what you pick is what that slot plays from then on.
The browser starts at /data/UserData/chompi-samples:
Built-in      the module's own wavs (the CHOMPI card set)
User Library  your own files, already on the Move
Copy WAV or AIFF files to User Library however you like; they show
up in the browser, and any rate, bit depth or channel count plays.
An assignment is kept per mode, bank and slot, and survives a
reload of the chain. Clear Slot puts the slot back to the built-in
sample it shipped with.
Slot 15 is the recording buffer - assign to slots 1-14.

children.title: JAMMI and CUBBI
lines: CUBBI: one slot per octave of the keybed (see the first topic), so
up to two different samples play at once on the 32 pads.
JAMMI: one sample plays the WHOLE keybed, pitched by the key. The C
in the middle of the two octaves is the sample at its own speed;
the pads below it play it slower, the ones above it faster. The
Slot knob chooses which sample that is.
Mode and Bank are on the Setup page. Each slot remembers its own
Tape page values (attack, decay, start, end, loop, gain, pan), so
changing slots changes what those knobs show and do.

children.title: Tape, looper, recorder
lines: Tape: the CHOMPI tape controls - reverse, sustain, auto-loop,
attack, decay, start, end, gain, pan - applied to the slot's
sample. They are remembered per slot.
Looper: records the module's output into a 60 s buffer, plays it
back with pitch/scrub/dub controls. Loop Rec starts it, Loop Play
starts playback, Clear Loop empties it.
Recorder: Chompi Rec records the audio input (Input, In Gain) to
temp_rec.wav, which lands in slot 15 - the keybed's buffer.
Monitor passes the input through to the output.
